checks.label: HTTPS
checks.source: RFC 9110 §4.2.2 (https URI scheme); OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet; auditmysite #775 (final URL decides)
checks.applicability: Applies to every audited URL that answered: the scheme of the final URL after redirects is the transport. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation:
Fails when the final URL of the fetched document is not https:. A certificate the client cannot validate is no HTTPS: the fetch fails and nothing is measured (errored), it never passes. An https: response validated against the trusted roots passes.

Always applicable: every fetched URL has a scheme. Note: the corpus serves on 127.0.0.1, which Secure Contexts ('Is origin potentially trustworthy?') treats as potentially trustworthy; the check deliberately judges the scheme, since an audit of a local build stands in for the deployed site.
